_comment: EXPLORATORY post hoc ablation (not pre-registered; not part of the pre-registered test). Ours-v2 and B9+ re-run on d1_open test with only the belief inputs replaced (and Ours-v2's belief-transition model refitted on dev for the oracle beliefs); alias-graded outcomes; no LLM judge.
status: EXPLORATORY post hoc ablation (not pre-registered; not part of the pre-registered test)
gate: the frozen-belief variant reproduced contrasts_test.json per-item Delta[COMMIT] and Delta[SPECULATIVE] at both cells to 1e-12

belief_variants.oracle: b_k = empirical need label y (0/1) at every step from the first partial
belief_variants.sharpen: b_k = p0 + f_k (y - p0), f_k = causal e/(e+R_hat) (1 at end of turn), p0 = dev base rate
belief_variants.reveal: b_k = p0 until f_k >= u_i, then y (u_i ~ U(0,1) from a hash of the item id): calibrated, sharpening; added by the analyst after `sharpen` proved miscalibrated at intermediate steps

dev_prior_source: mean of the E1-v2 dev empirical-need labels (d1_open, alias)

refitted.what: Ours-v2 belief-transition (lookahead) model only, per oracle variant
refitted.phase_variable: causal f_k (the frozen fit used the reference word fraction)

not_refitted: B9+ timing rule (frozen dev-tuned, belief-independent r_below / r_threshold rule), B9+ policy constants, prices, g+/g-, rho table, remaining-speech predictor, latency model

generation.grading: alias match only (d1_open scorer of record); no LLM judge or Azure call
generation.cost_note: GPU cost was not metered: GPU time = this wall time x the number of serving containers, which Phase A does not record (64 requests in flight).

summary_md: This ablation is exploratory and post hoc, not part of the pre-registered test: Ours-v2 and B9+ are re-run on the d1_open test items with only the belief replaced. With the empirical need label as the belief (oracle), the primary-cell contrast changes sign: Δ[COMMIT] = Δ[SPEC] = +0.0132 [+0.0081, +0.0184], against -0.0367 [-0.0481, -0.0252] with the real belief; both controllers then retrieve exactly the needed items and the gain comes from dispatch timing (Δ accuracy +0.0103, Δ latency term -0.0029), with zero interaction because no information arrives during the turn. With a calibrated belief that reveals the label at a random point of the utterance (a variant added by the analyst), joint control still wins (Δ[COMMIT] +0.0125 [+0.0070, +0.0180], Δ[SPEC] +0.0166 [+0.0108, +0.0224]), and the interaction is -0.0041 [-0.0064, -0.0019], the opposite sign to the P2 prediction. With the requested sharpening belief p0 + f (y − p0), which is informative but not calibrated mid-utterance, Ours-v2[COMMIT] commits early on intermediate beliefs and retrieves for 98.5% of the not-needed items (Δ[COMMIT] -0.0555 [-0.0668, -0.0444]), while Ours-v2[SPEC] decides exactly as under the oracle (Δ[SPEC] +0.0132 [+0.0081, +0.0184]). On text150 the oracle and reveal beliefs make Ours-v2 worse (Δ[COMMIT] -0.0927 [-0.1038, -0.0817] and -0.0428 [-0.0523, -0.0334]): with the dev-fitted g− = -0.112, the frozen objective values a fully hidden retrieval at f = 0.7 for an item known not to need it at +0.0009, so Ours-v2 takes it (80.8% of such items under the oracle) and pays in accuracy and latency. Taken together, the ablation suggests that the pre-registered negative result reflects the belief (and objective terms such as g−) more than the joint decision structure, but it does not show that a realistic belief reaches the regime where joint control pays: it is post hoc, on one dataset and price cell, alias-graded, with B9+'s timing rule tuned under the real belief, and the gain it finds is small.
caveats_md: Exploratory and post hoc: designed after the pre-registered d1_open analysis; it is not part of PREREG_V2 and changes none of its tests. The 'calibrated reveal' variant was added by the analyst after seeing that the requested sharpening belief is miscalibrated mid-utterance.

One dataset (d1_open), one latency profile and price per condition (the frozen primary cell and text150's own 0.65-quantile price), alias grading only (no LLM judge); items are the bootstrap clusters.

Only the belief and Ours-v2's lookahead transitions change. B9+ keeps the timing rule tuned on dev under the REAL belief (r_below on ASR, r_threshold on text150); a rule re-tuned under the oracle belief could do better, so the oracle contrasts may favour Ours-v2. g+/g−, ρ, prices and the remaining-speech predictor are the frozen dev fits; text150 uses the g+/g− fitted on the primary ASR condition, which is what drives its negative oracle result.

The oracle is the empirical need label (closed-book wrong on the text question in ≥ 3 of 5 draws); it is hindsight information no deployable controller has, and it is not the per-turn outcome (ASR-condition answers with or without passages), so 'perfect' refers to the label, not to the realised gain of retrieval.

Newly generated cells (Mistral-7B, same Phase A code path) were measured on 2026-10-18, the frozen ones on 2026-10-16, on the same endpoint and model; vLLM sampling with fixed seeds is reproducible per request but not guaranteed bit-identical across server batches, so these cells are comparable to, not identical with, cells the frozen run would have produced.
